title: Understanding urbanisation through geographical concepts
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:17Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:41Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The new point asks students to use the five geographical concepts together to explain where cities grow, what they are like, how they link to rural areas and whether growth lasts, and no bank point covers that; the closest, urban growth and urbanisation, only defines the terms and measures them.

draft.title: Urbanisation and geographical concepts
card: Space is where cities grow and how they are spread out, such as along a coast or a river. Place is what a city is like, including its people, buildings, land and feel.
Cities link to other places. Rural areas send food, water and workers to a city. The city sends back goods, services and money.
Change is how a city differs over time. Its population, size and land use can grow or shift across the years.
Sustainability asks whether a city's growth can last. It looks at whether the needs of people now can be met without harming the needs of people later.
draft.remember: Use space, place, interconnection, change and sustainability as questions to ask about any city.

a.q: A student asks how farms outside a city supply it with food and how the city sends goods back. Which concept is this?
a.why: Interconnection is about links between places, here a city and its rural areas. Space is tempting, but it is about where a city is and how it is spread out, not the links between places.
a.clue: Look for the word that means links between places.

b.q: Geographers study Wyndham in Victoria. They compare maps from 1990 and today to see how its suburbs have spread. Which concept does this mainly show?
b.why: Comparing maps from two dates shows how the city has differed over time, which is change. Sustainability is tempting, but it asks whether growth can last, and the maps alone only show that growth has happened.
b.clue: What does comparing two dates show about the city?
